verdict.root_cause: checkoutservice is healthy; its one failing step is an outbound HTTP POST to emailservice:6060 /send_order_confirmation that fails at DNS resolution against the container's embedded resolver (127.0.0.11:53) before any TCP dial. The same host/port/path succeeded earlier in the window, so the configured URL is not wrong — emailservice disappeared from service discovery some time between 21:37:09 and 21:49:29. The email step is non-fatal, so payment, cart, shipping and the orders publish all succeed and the error ratio peaks near 7.8% rather than going total. What removed emailservice from DNS (failed deploy, OOM kill, scale-to-zero, discovery-side change) was never dispatched on, so the initiating act is unestablished.
verdict.reasoning: tr_d05bec9e4467 pins the mechanism as name-lookup failure before connection, ruling out timeout/overload, connection refused, TLS, HTTP 4xx/5xx, and a mis-typed host/port/path (so bad_config is not the mechanism). tr_6dae66117de6 isolates the ERROR to that single short span and clears all core gRPC dependencies, the frontend, and the async pipeline; the span carries almost no duration, so this is not a waiting failure. tr_3377e25035db bounds impact to a partial excursion, inconsistent with checkoutservice crash-looping or exhausting resources. tr_7a44508803f5 and tr_5ec6c6704874 clear a checkoutservice change but queried only that service over ~15 minutes, so they say nothing about emailservice. With the caller exonerated and the callee never examined, the mechanism is a dependency absent from name resolution, but bad_deploy and resource_exhaustion on emailservice both produce this exact signature.
open_questions: Why did emailservice stop resolving? Its logs, container state, and change history were never dispatched.
